summary: The bill requires federal banking and credit union agencies to streamline de novo bank and credit union applications by reviewing forms, pulling data from other agencies, assigning caseworkers for guidance, offering mentor lists from recently approved institutions, consulting states and stakeholders on reforms, and issuing annual reports, while cutting the Federal Reserve's surplus fund by $24 million starting in 2036.

scores.thoughts: The bill's only fiscal provision (section 7) reduces the Federal Reserve's discretionary surplus fund by $24 million effective 2036. This is a minor, one-time reduction in funds available to the government and appears intended as an offset for the regulatory reforms in the rest of the bill. The core substance of the legislation is regulatory streamlining rather than appropriations or spending programs, so the effect is tangential and small in magnitude.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, tax policy, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms. It addresses bank chartering and regulatory processes only.
No provisions relate to health insurance, medical providers, public health programs, or healthcare markets.

No provisions address immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant rights.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.

The minor reduction in the Fed surplus fund has a negligible and indirect effect on Treasury receipts; the bill does not engage with deficit spending, debt ceiling, or debt-reduction strategies in any substantive way.
